source_review.notes: Checked current Linux cgroup-v2 and PSI documentation; current Kubernetes resource, CPU, memory, topology, QoS, and eviction documentation; current Docker and systemd controls; and primary Heracles, Borg, and Mesos publications. All thirteen final cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Interface claims are attributed and generic isolation recommendations state their scope.

evidence: Reviewed node capacity C, system reserve S, allocatable A, workload request r, cap m, weight w, placement P, and usage u(t).
Reviewed CPU/memory/I/O dimensions, device byte/operation caps, latency/pressure, victim objective O, interference delta, and tolerance epsilon.
Checked CPU, GiB, MiB/s, bytes, operations, time, weights, vectors, topology, and objective direction are explicit.
Confirmed requests, weights, caps, protection thresholds, affinity, and hard limits retain different semantics.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Conceptual symbols span platform-specific interfaces only where the chapter explicitly acknowledges semantic differences.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 admission fixture and reproduced allocatable (28,112,900), post-request (26,104,750), headroom (2,8,150), and admit True.
Recomputed Exercise 2 allocatable (42,224,1700), post-request (40,232,1600), and headroom (2,-8,100).
Verified Exercise 2 rejects on the 8-GiB memory deficit despite spare CPU and I/O.
Checked resource vectors use consistent units within each dimension and never substitute one resource for another.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Request-vector examples prove simplified admission only, not burst containment, topology feasibility, or runtime service objectives.

evidence: Verified A=C-S and componentwise request admission sum(r)+r_new <= A under declared effective capacity.
Verified a leaf CPU weight cannot overcome an ancestor bandwidth cap because the parent bounds service offered to all descendants.
Checked aggregate memory protection cannot be absolute when effective protections exceed physical allocatable memory.
Verified interference delta compares matched colocated and solo outcomes with a declared lower-is-better objective.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter explicitly limits inference to modeled dimensions and tested workload/topology conditions.

evidence: Reviewed idle/full CPUs, fractional/exclusive cores, short bursts, ancestor caps, SMT, interrupts, NUMA, cache, bandwidth, power, and thermal sharing.
Reviewed anonymous/native/file/kernel/socket/tmpfs/shared memory, zero headroom, reclaim, swap, dirty writeback, high/max thresholds, and group/node OOM.
Reviewed buffered/direct I/O, wrong/stacked devices, local/network/object storage, queue depth, remote quotas, checkpoint bursts, and device failure.
Reviewed process escape, privileged mutation, runtime/controller restart, resize below use, hotplug, telemetry loss, malicious under-requesting, and node-agent starvation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Performance, node survival, fairness, security, correctness, and economics are reviewed as distinct boundaries.

evidence: Traced physical capacity through system reserve, allocatable advertisement, request admission, hierarchy, runtime controls, pressure, and remediation.
Checked every process/descendant remains charged through tenant/job/task hierarchy and actual leaf behavior stays bounded by ancestors.
Checked CPU weight/cap/cpuset, memory protection/high/max/OOM, and I/O weight/max bind distinct mechanisms and observed paths.
Checked task attempts, spill/shuffle/checkpoint/state, fencing, scheduler recovery, and policy generations remain connected to node events.
invariant_checking.notes: No enforcement claim is made for remote storage or uncore resources without a corresponding path or placement mechanism.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from objective/threat model and reserve through enforcement, observability, adaptation, and adversarial validation.
Checked request-fit proof depends on trustworthy requests, correct allocatable capacity, and modeled topology/dimensions.
Checked hierarchy counterexamples for high child weight under capped parent and overcommitted memory protections.
Checked empirical isolation inference is bounded to tested workload versions, phases, concurrency, topology, devices, and controller configuration.
proof_review.notes: No universal performance-isolation theorem is claimed; residual shared resources require measurement or avoided co-location.

evidence: Audited request, reservation, weight, share, cap, maximum, protection, affinity, exclusive, allocatable, usage, pressure, throttle, reclaim, and OOM.
Confirmed logical CPU is not mislabeled physical core and CPU-time isolation is not mislabeled cache/memory-bandwidth isolation.
Confirmed RSS/heap/current charge are not mislabeled complete working set and page cache is not labeled free.
Confirmed local block-I/O control is not mislabeled end-to-end remote-storage isolation and utilization is not labeled contention.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Claims consistently name enforcement layer, resource type, topology, and runtime versus admission semantics.

evidence: Reviewed effective configuration, usage, service, throttling, PSI, reclaim/fault/OOM, dirty/writeback, device/network latency/queue, and task/stage outcomes.
Confirmed no universal CPU period/cap, memory request/high/max, swap, I/O weight/max, reserve, pressure threshold, or interference tolerance is prescribed.
Confirmed the executable fixture demonstrates admission arithmetic only and is not evidence for runtime isolation or production performance.
Confirmed acceptance requires solo baselines, one-dimensional and compound aggressors, real phases/topology, failures, canary, and rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Isolation evidence includes protected-victim outcomes, aggressor progress, node survival, fairness, utilization, and cost.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed objectives/threats, node reserves, requests/limits, hierarchy, CPU weights/caps/affinity, complete memory accounting/protection/OOM/cache, I/O enforcement/remote paths, NUMA/uncore, dataflow phases, resize, pressure, gaming, and empirical validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable capacity inventory, cgroup hierarchy, system reservations, effective-state reconciliation, throttling/PSI/reclaim/OOM/writeback telemetry, device-path resolution, NUMA coordination, phase-aware policies, bounded feedback, escape testing, canary, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from resource semantics through each enforcement mechanism and coupled dataflow effects. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover reserves, weights, quotas, complete memory, page cache, writeback, remote storage, NUMA, resize, executable admission, design, diagnosis, and rollout.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Linux/systemd/Docker/Kubernetes maintainer, Heracles/Borg/Mesos researcher, kernel/runtime/storage/network engineer, cluster/data-platform operator, SRE/security/FinOps specialist, affected tenant, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
